mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals Federal Reserve tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 195

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3pp rise in UNRATE over 3 months signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and HOUST above their 12-month moving averages indicate robust economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS and HOUST are both above their 12-month moving averages

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a 0.5% monthly decline in INDPRO signals industrial contraction, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 1 month during a monetary tightening cycle

mechanism_narrative: A higher HOUST (housing starts) level indicates strong consumer demand for housing, stimulating economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 2000

mechanism_narrative: A decline in INDPRO below 115 signals industrial contraction, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 115

mechanism_narrative: Combined CPIAUCSL > 195 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0 signal aggressive monetary tightening, increasing cost of capital and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 195 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0

mechanism_narrative: During high labor market slack (UNRATE > 5.5%), a 0.5% monthly decline in PAYEMS signals worsening employment, reducing consumer spending and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines > 0.5% in 1 month and UNRATE > 5.5%
